card.title: Diagnosing iPhone “No IMEI / No Service” via RFFE Bus Analysis with ESP32

source.title: Diagnosing iPhone “No IMEI / No Service” via RFFE Bus Analysis with ESP32

claims.statement: A phone that boots normally but shows no IMEI on *#06# and no service, even after a clean restore, can be caused by an RF power amplifier not answering on the RFFE bus rather than by the baseband CPU or BBPMU.
claims.evidence: Guide describes RFFE scanning with an ESP32.

claims.statement: An ESP32 flashed with an RFFE scanner can be wired to a bus (D22=SCL, D21=SDA, GND, 3V3 pin to the board's 1.8 V line) to list which PA addresses respond (1) or not (0).
claims.evidence: Example output marks address 0x3 as not responding.

claims.statement: iPhone 12 / 12 Pro has 8 separate RFFE buses, so each bus must be scanned in turn.
claims.evidence: Test point maps per model are required.

claims.statement: A non-responding PA is usually a faulty PA module; sometimes the break is in the interposer (sandwich) signal path.
claims.evidence: Continuity test CPU to interposer to PA.

procedure: Confirm no service with a known-good SIM and no IMEI on *#06#; restore to rule out software.
Inspect for prior interposer work, liquid near the RF section and PA modules.
Flash the ESP32 with the RFFE scanner firmware.
Solder SDA, SCL, 1.8 V and GND to the RFFE test points for one bus.
Scan; note any address returning 0; repeat for every bus.
Replace the non-responding PA or repair the interposer path; check continuity.
card.caveats: Requires model-specific RFFE test point maps; downloads referenced by the guide are third-party. Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
